title: More Fruits for Kids! Grapes, Pear, Kiwi and More with Pip
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Pip the strawberry, and this is my buddy Kiko the broccoli!
Welcome to Fruity Friends! Today we're meeting five fruity friends that grow on trees and vines.
Can you count with me? One, two, three, four, five!
Yummy food and healthy habits help us grow, play and learn every day.
Ready? Let's go to the kitchen and find out!

lines: Here's a clue: they're small and round, and they grow together in a big bunch! Can you guess?
This is Grapes! Can you say grapes?
Grapes grow on long, twisty plants called vines. They hang down in big, heavy bunches.
Grapes can be green, red or purple. And raisins are grapes that dried in the sun!
Can you make a bunch of grapes? Hold up your fingers and wiggle them, one, two, three!
How do grown-ups get grapes ready for little kids?
They cut them into small pieces, so they're easy to eat!
One more time, nice and loud: GRAPES!
Grapes are sweet and juicy, and they make a cool, crunchy snack.
Here's a clue: it's skinny at the top, round at the bottom, and it grows on a tree! Can you guess?
This is Pear! Can you say pear?
Pears grow on trees, just like apples do. They can be green, yellow, brown or red.
A pear is ready when it feels a little soft near the top, by the stem.
Can you make a pear shape? Hands up high and skinny, then make your tummy round!
What's hiding in the middle of a pear?
Little brown seeds! A new pear tree could grow from one.
One more time, nice and loud: PEAR!
Pears are soft and sweet, and so juicy you might need a napkin!
Here's a clue: it's brown and fuzzy outside, but it's a big surprise inside! Can you guess?
This is Kiwi! Can you say kiwi?
A kiwi has fuzzy brown skin, a little bit like a teddy bear.
But inside, it's bright green, with a ring of tiny black seeds. And yes, you can eat the seeds!
Can you pretend to scoop a kiwi with a spoon? Scoop, scoop, yum!
What color is a kiwi on the inside?
Bright green! With tiny black seeds all around.
One more time, nice and loud: KIWI!
Kiwis taste sweet and a little bit tangy, all at the same time.
Here's a clue: they're little and red, and they often come in pairs with long stems! Can you guess?
This is Cherries! Can you say cherries?
Cherries grow on trees. In spring, the trees are covered in pretty pink and white flowers.
Later, the flowers turn into shiny red cherries, hanging by their long stems.
Can you hold up two fingers, like a pair of cherries? Wiggle, wiggle!
What's in the middle of a cherry?
A hard pit! A grown-up takes it out for you first.
One more time, nice and loud: CHERRIES!
Cherries are sweet, shiny and red, like little jewels.
Here's a clue: it's round and fuzzy, and it can be orange, yellow and pink! Can you guess?
This is Peach! Can you say peach?
Peaches grow on trees. Their skin is soft and fuzzy, like a cozy blanket.
Inside, a peach is sweet and juicy, and it smells so yummy.
Can you rub your cheek gently, like soft peach fuzz? So soft!
What's in the middle of a peach?
A big, bumpy pit! A grown-up cuts around it for you.
One more time, nice and loud: PEACH!
A ripe peach is so juicy, it can drip right down your chin!

recap: Yummy! Let's remember what we learned.
Pear, skinny on top and round on the bottom.
Kiwi, fuzzy outside and green inside.
Cherries, with a pit in the middle.
outro: Which one was your favorite? Tell a grown-up, and try something new this week!
Bye, friends! See you next time on Fruity Friends!
